title: Any Word, PDF, or Photo Becomes a Norwegian Lesson | vitalii.no
description:
I wanted to learn Norwegian by ear during commutes and other dead time, but every listening app I tried made me pick from someone else's pre-recorded topics. I couldn't just say the word I actually needed, feed it a PDF from the textbook I was already using, or snap a photo of a page and have it read back to me at my own level.

So I built mini.vitalii.no as a Cloudflare Worker backed by a D1 database, where each requested topic becomes a row in a job queue. A VPS runner polls for pending topics and calls Claude to write the situation text with vocabulary and example sentences, edge-tts voices it, and ffmpeg mixes the tracks into four listening modes. Content is voiced section by section, so content grows incrementally and playback starts after the first section instead of waiting for the whole topic to render. I also added file upload as an input source: PDFs read directly, scanned pages and photos OCR'd, plus common document formats, all usable as either the lesson text itself or as source material for a generated lesson.

A lesson now starts playing back within about a minute, instead of waiting for the whole thing to render. Four listening modes and adjustable per-topic repeats mean the same material can be replayed for pure listening or for parallel translation without regenerating anything.
